explanation.headline: Fold was close: within 0.37 bb of the top play, Raise 2.5x.

paragraphs: You held 4♣ K♥ on the button, against Villain, a LAG player, in the big blind. It was your turn to act with 1.5 bb in the pot.
sections.title: The hand

paragraphs: You chose Fold (EV 0 bb). The top play was Raise 2.5x (EV 0.37 bb), so your choice gives up 0.37 bb against Villain's range. That is close to the top play, so the verdict is Fine.
Your equity against Villain's whole range is 52.2%.

Raise 2.5x: Villain folds 16% of the time, less than the 57.1% a raise this size needs to profit on folds alone (2 bb / (1.5 bb + 2 bb)), so folds alone don't pay for it: it relies on your 49.4% equity against the hands that continue.
Right now you are ahead of 70.9% of Villain's range.
sections.title: The verdict

paragraphs: Villain is a LAG player. Loose-aggressive: wide ranges, frequent pressure, more bluffs.
Villain had not acted yet, so the range is every hand Villain can hold.
The range in the Range tab is the range this puzzle was graded on.

simplifications.text: Pre-flop, Villain's responses don't depend on Hero's raise size.
Before the river, Hero is assumed to realise a share of equity set by position: in position 100%; out of position 80% pre-flop, 88% on the flop, 94% on the turn. All-in pots realise 100%.
After a Villain re-raise, Hero only folds or calls.
